records.description: Use for placeholder content before user input is provided. Pair with the matching background token when text appears inside a semantic state container.
notFor: Static helper text or hints displayed below or near an input — use text/secondary.
Labels or any text that must persist after the user starts typing.
General muted or supporting copy — placeholder text semantically belongs inside form inputs only.

records.description: Use for disabled text where content belongs to unavailable UI and all interaction is halted; pair with disabled background, icon, and border tokens.
notFor: Decorative muted or low-emphasis text — use text/secondary for visual hierarchy.
Read-only inputs where users can still interact with the content — use text/read only.
Any element that can still receive focus, be copied, or be interacted with in any way.

records.description: Use for text in read-only interactive components where the value is visible but cannot be edited; unlike disabled, the component may still allow focus, selection, or copying. Do not use for static body copy.
notFor: Static page or body copy — use text/primary or text/secondary.
Fully disabled elements where all interaction is halted — use text/disabled.
Any non-form-input context — this token is specifically for read-only form fields.

Use for text that communicates the result of a failed user action — form validation errors, incorrect passwords, submission failures, or any inline feedback where the user made a mistake and needs to correct it. This is reactive: something already went wrong. Do not use for warning users about what might happen. text/error and text/danger share the same hex value intentionally — they are rarely used together, and even when they are, users do not need to distinguish them by color. The separation is semantic, for the author: choosing the right token makes the intent clear in code and in Figma.
notFor: Warnings or caution messages that appear before a user takes action — use text/warning or text/danger.
Destructive action confirmation text (e.g. delete dialogs) — use text/danger.
General red emphasis or visual decoration — this token carries error semantics and implies something went wrong.

records.description: Use for text placed on error semantic backgrounds to maintain sufficient color contrast; do not use on unrelated surface colors.

Use for text that signals a destructive or irreversible action — deleting a project, removing a user, permanently destroying data. This is proactive: you are warning the user before they act. Do not use for validation feedback or error messages after something went wrong; use text/error for those. text/danger and text/error share the same hex value intentionally — both deliver urgency and demand attention visually. They are rarely used together, and even when they are, users do not need to distinguish them by color. The separation is semantic, for the author: choosing the right token makes the intent clear in code and in Figma.
notFor: Validation feedback or error messages after a user action failed — use text/error.
General warnings or cautionary text that is not about destruction — use text/warning.
Red emphasis without a destructive action context.

notFor: Non-interactive text you want to style in blue — this token implies navigability or action.
Text inside buttons — use the appropriate on-brand or on-danger token.

records.name: Heading 01
records.description: Use for the highest-level page heading when strong brand-led hierarchy is needed; must be paired with text-brand in Via for now.

records.name: Heading 02
records.description: Use for major section headings below the page title when strong brand-led hierarchy is needed; must be paired with text-brand in Via for now.

records.name: Heading 03
records.description: Use for prominent section or panel headings that need clear hierarchy without the brand serif style.

records.name: Heading 04
records.description: Use for medium section headings, modal titles, or card headings within product UI.

records.name: Heading 05
records.description: Use for compact section headings or subsection titles in dense product UI.

records.name: Heading 06
records.description: Use for the smallest heading level when text represents heading hierarchy, such as compact group titles or dense section headings; do not use as a component label.

records.name: Body Large
records.description: Use for body copy that needs larger default readability; recommended as the base body font size for Edu experiences.

records.name: Body Medium
records.description: Use for default product UI body text, descriptions, and readable supporting content; recommended as the base body font size for non-Edu products.

records.name: Code Large
records.description: Use for larger code snippets, command examples, or monospace values that need more visual presence.

records.name: Code Medium
records.description: Use for default inline code, compact code snippets, command examples, or monospace values.

records.name: Label Large
records.description: Use only for large label text in component building, such as button labels, form labels, or control labels; do not use for body copy, headings, or decorative emphasis.

records.name: Label Medium
records.description: Use only for default label text in component building, such as button labels, form labels, table labels, or control labels; do not use for heading hierarchy, body copy, or general supporting text.

records.name: Label Small
records.description: Use only for compact label text in dense component UI, small controls, or constrained spaces; do not use for body copy, captions, or decorative emphasis.

records.name: Utility Description
records.description: Use for helper text, supplemental descriptions, and low-emphasis explanatory content near controls or settings; do not use for longer paragraphs.

records.name: Utility Disclaimer
records.description: Use for legal, compliance, or fine-print disclaimers that must remain readable but lower emphasis.
